Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}={x}^{4} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{4}\,dx=\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{{e}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)}{5}-\frac{{1}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{5}]-\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{1}^{e}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)}{5}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{25}{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{5}}{5}-(\frac{{e}^{5}}{25}-\frac{1}{25}) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(5{e}^{5}-{e}^{5}+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(4{e}^{5}+1).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9e0c4dfe-2a2c-535e-956d-62ad8cee8229"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9e0c4dfe-2a2c-535e-956d-62ad8cee8229" :answer-field/id #uuid "9e0c4dfe-2a2c-535e-956d-62ad8cee8229" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-1c2596bc-8831-5738-bc87-23664928dc31" :answer-field/choices ["answer-1c2596bc-8831-5738-bc87-23664928dc31"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c2596bc-8831-5738-bc87-23664928dc31" :answer/id #uuid "1c2596bc-8831-5738-bc87-23664928dc31" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{4e^5+1}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-45517c4f-34c5-5613-91b3-714b64a55e54" :question/id #uuid "45517c4f-34c5-5613-91b3-714b64a55e54" :question/math-academy-id "q-78972" :question/problem "$\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡2x\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡2x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-x+C \\  & =x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-8afc707b-a42b-5621-ace9-e6a014a201bb"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-8afc707b-a42b-5621-ace9-e6a014a201bb" :answer-field/id #uuid "8afc707b-a42b-5621-ace9-e6a014a201bb" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-612aede7-2fcb-5f05-9a9e-41d69e0a1e2c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-bd63e3cd-ff82-5ade-9211-594e2bfdb08c" "answer-cc74e90b-cf7b-5156-89e6-293ad43d67ea" "answer-1fac7b1b-401e-571f-9ac1-c8035cba4079" "answer-612aede7-2fcb-5f05-9a9e-41d69e0a1e2c" "answer-92b952c7-daa6-5ab4-a7f5-81b3cf909d3a"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bd63e3cd-ff82-5ade-9211-594e2bfdb08c" :answer/id #uuid "bd63e3cd-ff82-5ade-9211-594e2bfdb08c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1)+C" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cc74e90b-cf7b-5156-89e6-293ad43d67ea" :answer/id #uuid "cc74e90b-cf7b-5156-89e6-293ad43d67ea" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)+C" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1fac7b1b-401e-571f-9ac1-c8035cba4079" :answer/id #uuid "1fac7b1b-401e-571f-9ac1-c8035cba4079" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-612aede7-2fcb-5f05-9a9e-41d69e0a1e2c" :answer/id #uuid "612aede7-2fcb-5f05-9a9e-41d69e0a1e2c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-1)+C" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-92b952c7-daa6-5ab4-a7f5-81b3cf909d3a" :answer/id #uuid "92b952c7-daa6-5ab4-a7f5-81b3cf909d3a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186097927 :tutorial/content "Suppose that we want to evaluate the integral

$$
\int x\ln{x}\, \textrm{d}x \,.
$$

The method of integration by parts can help us solve this problem. Let's remind ourselves of the "by-parts" formula,

$$
\int u v' \textrm{d}x = uv - \int v u'\textrm{d}x.
$$

We usually let $u = x,$ but that would leave us with $v' = \ln(x)$ which is hard to integrate. So instead, we're going to choose our $u$ and $v'$ slightly differently, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now the formula of integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int {{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}_{⏟}}_{u}\cdot {{x}_{⏟}}_{{v}^{′}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}-\int \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

When we apply integration by parts to integrals containing logarithmic functions, we should *always* identify the logarithmic function with $u,$ not with $v'.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186096910 :activity/expected-seconds 1320.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

:tutorial/content "Suppose that we want to evaluate the integral

$$
\int x\ln{x}\, \textrm{d}x \,.
$$

The method of integration by parts can help us solve this problem. Let's remind ourselves of the "by-parts" formula,

$$
\int u v' \textrm{d}x = uv - \int v u'\textrm{d}x.
$$

We usually let $u = x,$ but that would leave us with $v' = \ln(x)$ which is hard to integrate. So instead, we're going to choose our $u$ and $v'$ slightly differently, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{'}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{'}=x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now the formula of integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\,\operatorname{ln}x\,\text{d}x & =\int {{\operatorname{ln}x}_{⏟}}_{u}\cdot {{x}_{⏟}}_{{v}^{'}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}-\int \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}x-\frac{1}{2}\int x\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}x-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

When we apply integration by parts to integrals containing logarithmic functions, we should *always* identify the logarithmic function with $u,$ not with $v'.$" :tutorial/id #uuid
